name: Shelf Patchwork Tank (Scavenged)
description:
Not a manufactured item — this is something built from nothing. A tank top assembled from three or four mismatched fabric sources: a section of old corporate uniform fabric (the logo partially burned or bleached out), a strip of fluorescent mesh from a construction vest, and a back panel that might be repurposed synth-bag material. Whoever made it knew what they were doing — the seams hold, the armholes are clean, and someone has added a hand-stitched border along the collar in a tight cross-stitch pattern using bright orange thread. Every one of these is unique.

On the Shelf, you wear what you can get. But there's craft here — real craft. Some of these tanks end up in Tier 3 boutiques with a four-hundred-quanta markup and a story about 'authentic street construction.' The people who made them don't see a coin of that.
what_it_says: You make do. You also make something out of making do — there's pride in this, even if the world doesn't see it that way.
worn_by: young people with nothing and style anyway
story_hooks: The burned-out logo on the front is from a corponation that was supposedly dissolved fifteen years ago — but someone is still making uniforms with that mark.
A Tier 4 fashion house has started producing 'authentic Shelf-inspired' reproductions of this style, and the backlash from Tier 1 communities is building toward something uglier than protest.
A character recognizes the cross-stitch pattern as a specific maker's signature — and that maker disappeared six months ago.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately deconstructed tank top that reads as intentional rather than accidental. The patchwork composition creates visual rhythm across the torso—corporate formality interrupted by construction-grade neon, grounded by salvaged utility material. The silhouette is relaxed but structured enough to hold shape; the hand-stitched collar detail draws the eye upward and suggests maker identity rather than factory anonymity.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the shoulders and torso with minimal taper at the sides. Armholes cut generous but finished cleanly. Length hits mid-hip on most frames. Not oversized, but deliberately unstreamlined—allows for layering or movement without clinging.
physical_description.primary_material: Mixed-source composite: section of degraded corporate synthetic-cotton blend (faded, slightly stiff), fluorescent mesh polyester (construction-grade, high visibility), and recycled synth-leather or treated polymer bag material (back panel, slightly waxy texture)
physical_description.texture: Tactilely varied by design. Corporate section has a worn, almost papery hand from repeated washing or chemical exposure. Mesh is open-weave and slightly scratchy, with visible grid pattern. Back panel is smooth, slightly plastic-like, possibly with subtle creasing or fold marks from its previous life. Hand-stitched collar border is slightly raised and textured from thick orange thread pulled taut through each X-stitch.
physical_description.color_scheme: Muted base palette with violent accents. Corporate section in faded steel-gray or corporate blue (heavily desaturated). Mesh in electric lime or safety orange (almost radioactive). Back panel in charcoal or weathered black-gray. Hand-stitched border in bright signal orange—the only truly saturated accent that catches light.
physical_description.closures: None—pulls over the head. Clean, finished neckline despite patchwork construction suggests intentional design rather than accident.
distinctive_features: Visible seam lines between three distinct fabric panels—slightly raised and stitched with precision
Hand-stitched cross-stitch border around neckline in bright orange thread, consistent and tight
Partial ghost image or bleached logo shadow on corporate-fabric section (barely visible, adds authenticity)
Fluorescent mesh section semi-transparent, shows skin or undergarment beneath
Minor color variation and wear patterns suggest individual construction, no two identical
Back panel possibly retains subtle creases or manufacturing marks from previous use
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 origin (salvage/ungoverned construction) masquerading in Tier 3 markets; worn by people who either made it themselves or sourced it directly from makers. Tier 2 fashion tourists might pay inflated prices for 'authenticity,' unaware of actual tier context.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street-tier indicator—signals maker culture, resource ingenuity, and refusal of corporate supply chains. Worn by salvagers, Shelf residents, DIY augmentation techs, and people who value craft over consistency. Also worn ironically by corpo aesthetes seeking 'authentic street authenticity' at boutique markup. The wearer's actual tier is ambiguous—could be someone making do, or someone making a statement.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in from wear but structurally sound. Seams hold without puckering. Collar border may show slight fading depending on wearer's sun exposure and laundry habits. Mesh may have minor snags but remains functional. No intentional distressing—any wear is genuine use-wear.
